terms.gloss: a check mark (in Traupman, marking an error)
evidence: Quint. 1.4.3 (Lewis & Short s.v. virgula: “censoria, a critical mark, as a sign of spuriousness”)
terms.comment: The phrase is Quintilian’s, but for the critic’s stroke set against a spurious line (the obelus); Traupman uses it for the mark a teacher makes against a mistake, a modern sense.

terms.gloss: mark with a check mark, check off
terms.comment: Traupman prints vigulā, a misprint; to check off is simply notāre; to mark an error, virgulā cēnsōriā notāre.

sources: Lewis & Short: noto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 289; p. 290.
